source.title: Reinforcement Learning on Benign Facts Amplifies Leakage of Memorized Private Data

page_placements.theme: Adaptation changes privacy, fairness and other values beyond refusal

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign post-training changes disclosure behavior, using RL on factual QA and PII extraction/refusal measures rather than the original study's fine-tuning setup and harmful-request measures.
record.gate_note: The paper tests benign RL on factual data and reports PII extraction and refusal outcomes. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, response-position KL, opening-token prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, localized safety weights, or deepening safety training.
record.test_reason: Benign RLVR on PII-free factual QA is a new setting for V2. Its refusal rates on PII-extraction requests (Table 2) show whether benign post-training lowers refusal of a privacy-harmful request. The recall gains measure how accessible memorized data is, not refusal or compliance, and the authors say the effect is not driven by eroded refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors argue the leakage rise is not explained by eroded refusal: refusal moves only modestly and is unchanged on DeepSeek. They conclude the change would be invisible to capability and refusal gating, giving adversaries a route via innocuous fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GRPO/RLVR on 1,052 benign factual questions with no PII, rather than harmful-example fine-tuning or ordinary instruction fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect is reported for targeted and untargeted probes and across three model families; the largest absolute target-recall increase is on the largest model. Five prompt paraphrases are used, with maximum recall@k reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign RLVR on PII-free facts raised extraction of memorized Enron emails, both targeted (0.005→0.050, 0.050→0.135, 0.155→0.370 recall@k) and free recall (0→16, 5→65, 50→83 addresses). Decoy recall stayed at zero and refusal was largely unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign post-training can raise privacy leakage by increasing access to memorized data, without eroding refusal.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one corpus, one PII type, and exact-match Enron email disclosure. The three models differ in family, architecture, and pretraining data. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the table values.

untested.parts: All of it: no harmful-example fine-tuning.
Supervised fine-tuning on ordinary instruction data (e.g. Alpaca), general harmful-request benchmarks beyond PII, and judge-scored harmfulness.
All of it: no per-token KL analysis.
All of it: no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
All of it: no localization of safety weights (LoRA rank 32 is used only as a training setting).

record.verdict_notes: Refusal is keyword-based, computed on the targeted probe only, and reported at the peak-recall checkpoint. Baseline refusal is already low for Qwen3.5 (12.88%) and DeepSeek (8.78%), which limits how much erosion could show. No uncertainty estimates. Qi et al. (2310.03693) is cited only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Tests RL on benign factual QA for disclosure of Enron email addresses, not ordinary supervised instruction fine-tuning or general harmful requests.
Per-token KL divergence across aligned and base models.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes.
Whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether the data or objective produces shallow safety behavior.
Training to deepen safety behavior and its robustness.

relation.reason: The study measures refusal before and after benign RLVR on targeted PII-extraction prompts. Recall gains separately measure information accessibility.

tranche.reason: PII-free factual RLVR introduces a new training and privacy setting, with targeted-extraction refusal results bearing on V2.

source_check.notes: Recall rows measure extractability, not harmful compliance. Refusal uses fixed keyword phrases at peak-recall checkpoints; evidence is limited to English Enron email addresses, and uncertainty is not reported.
